coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 non-blocking advisories. Eighteen attacks run; the one that landed is advisory-grade. Custody is intact: turn-2 subject a7b44ff6 at 0444 unmoved, turn-1 subject frozen at 722bf2ea, HEAD never left 5b6f723, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all eight measured-inputs rows reproduce including both turn-1 verdicts. Both SHOULD-FIX landed, and I tested them by re-deriving rather than by reading the repair table. D-134-SF-1: Decision 1 now enumerates the 21 rows, states cardinality 23, and expressly holds DR-128/129/130 on the deferral limb. The sharpest risk the repair introduced is a mis-transcription, so I compared the new enumeration element-by-element and in order against D-002's own paragraph — identical, 21 of 21, no insertion, omission or reordering. The inaccurate 'D-002/D-010' compound survives at exactly one place, the deferral limb, where it is correct. D-134-SF-2: 'D-018 §2' now appears zero times; the entry rests on D-002's ownership of the set plus D-132 clause 3, both verified verbatim at their live locations, and cites D-018 item 2 only for the six sets it names, with an express disclaimer. That is a stronger repair than I asked for, because it drops the D-018 authority claim rather than explaining an inference. I also tested something the entry asserts without showing: that adding two rows implies no condition-4 gate-set amendment. It passes — the foreseeable remainders route to DR-G01..G05, G10, G12, G20 and G21, all already inside D-002's required set — which matters because D-133's gate 3 makes a named gate a precondition for either row ever becoming SATISFIED. The two advisories are that both of my turn-1 advisories are missing from the disposition table, one of them having been silently acted on, and that the gate check above is worth recording. Neither blocks. The entry is adoptable.
